analyst_view.overall: Leaders Arsenal (27 points, five straight league wins) visit 12th-placed Newcastle, who have one win in their last five league games and drew 1-1 at Fulham before the international break, and Matthias Jaissle's side lost 1-0 at home to Everton earlier this month. Arteta confirmed on Friday that Zubimendi is out for a few weeks with a hamstring injury picked up with Spain (until now he was only a doubt), Saka (quad) is still about four weeks away, and Max Dowman serves the last game of his ban after the FA rejected Arsenal's appeal; the numbers already have all three out. Saliba is fit again but Arteta wants to build his minutes gradually after only 45 minutes for the Under-21s, so a full start is not certain. Newcastle are without Joelinton (thigh) and goalkeeper Jaouen, both counted, while Ramsey is back from his ban, Fernandez-Pardo is over a virus, Willock and Nico Gonzalez are back from illness and Livramento may return. Referee Chris Kavanagh (4.5 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 11% off Arsenal for Saka and lowering Newcastle for their poor scoring lately (6 goals in six). This morning I leaned a little lower because of Saliba's return, but Arteta now says Saliba's minutes will be built up slowly and Zubimendi is definitely out, which takes some control out of Arsenal's midfield; with Newcastle getting Ramsey, Willock and Fernandez-Pardo back, those pull in both directions, so I move back to 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Arsenal pin teams back and both sides are dangerous from set pieces, but that is in their ratings and recent counts (Arsenal 36 corners in six games), and Zubimendi's absence is not the kind of change that alters how much either side attacks down the flanks, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already adding about 21% for referee Chris Kavanagh and more for both sides' busier recent card counts. A home crowd frustrated with Jaissle and an Arsenal midfield without its usual holding man could mean more fouls, but that is a hunch the counts mostly cover already, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, already raised for Newcastle conceding plenty of shots lately and Arsenal's steady volume. Arsenal without Zubimendi may control the ball a little less, which could give Newcastle's returning midfielders more chances to break, while Arsenal's attack is unchanged from what the numbers assume; nothing clear either way, so I keep 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target, already lowered for Newcastle's poor recent accuracy (21 on target in six). Saka's absence is counted and the only new forward news is Fernandez-Pardo being available again after a virus, which is too small to move it, so I stay at 7.8.
